verdicts.trueWording: ce choix de traduction diminue à mon avis l’effet
verdicts.note: Thesis PDF fetched and text-extracted; footnote 42 carries the quoted words verbatim and continues that the choice weakens the effect the legendary name produces in the reader's imagination (Vonarburg rendering Guinevere as 'Geneviève' not 'Guenièvre'). Author, Université Laval, 2013 confirmed on the title page.

verdicts.trueWording: I’ll use punctuation varaibly depending on context, speaker, rhythms.
verdicts.note: Ysabel journal, post of Thursday, September 14, 2006 on proofreading. Quoted sentence appears word for word, including the page's own typo 'varaibly', after his complaint about a proofreader over-punctuating speech.

verdicts.trueWording: LAST LIGHT is punctuated differently than the MOSAIC was.
verdicts.note: Same September 14, 2006 proofreading post, the sentence immediately following the punctuation-variably line. The page uses the shorthand caps titles LAST LIGHT and MOSAIC for The Last Light of the Sun and the Sarantine Mosaic.

verdicts.trueWording: comma, semi-colon, paragraph break, tense shift, word-choice wars
verdicts.note: Children of Earth and Sky category page. The phrase appears verbatim in the post describing his review of copy-editor Catherine Marjoribanks's pass, with the surrounding paragraph on marginalia dialogues and 'stet' confirming these are his exchanges with her.

verdicts.trueWording: Hearing a reading aloud isn’t reading a book.
verdicts.note: Under Heaven tour journal, post of Sunday, April 25, 2010, in the passage on touring and 'the sharing'. The sentence appears word for word; the next sentence adds that hearing an author interviewed is not either, but they can shed light.

verdicts.trueWording: what works when you are reading alone to yourself is not
verdicts.note: Ysabel journal, post of Monday, November 20, 2006 on his first public reading from Ysabel. The quoted words appear verbatim and the sentence completes with the same-as/listening-in-public contrast the claim states.

verdicts.trueWording: producer ‘would like to have Simon Vance do the reading’
verdicts.note: Under Heaven tour journal, post of Thursday, February 18, 2010. The quoted words are on the page verbatim, and the Tigana / Fionavar trilogy limb is fully supported. But the post reports an email from Penguin USA that the audio book's producer WOULD LIKE Vance to read; Kay says he is 'completely onside' and that they will be going into studio soon. Vance is named only this once in the whole journal, so the page records a proposal, not a completed reading of Under Heaven.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that Simon Vance actually read Under Heaven — the page records only the producer's request and a not-yet-started studio session

verdicts.trueWording: I’m not an audio book person
verdicts.note: Same February 18, 2010 post, opening the paragraph after the Vance news; the page continues that a growing number of friends and professional contacts are.

verdicts.trueWording: you are reading someone else’s rendering of me
verdicts.note: Ysabel journal, October 2006 post (between the October 14 and October 8, 2006 entries) on translation and the Giller Prize. The page's conditional names Russian, Korean and Portuguese exactly as the claim does.

verdicts.trueWording: It is a version, an interpretation, of that person’s work.
verdicts.note: Same October 2006 Ysabel translation post; the sentence closes the paragraph arguing that a translated work should not be treated as purely the original author's and that a mediating translator's voice exists.

verdicts.trueWording: the gift or the burden of the people who carry my work
verdicts.note: Same October 2006 Ysabel post; the full clause reads that he feels 'alternatively' the gift or the burden of the people who carry his work over into another language. The claim's 'alternately' is the only wording difference and does not change the sense.

verdicts.trueWording: la traduction, pour une écrivaine, c’est encore de l’écriture
verdicts.note: Diacritik interview headlined 'Fiat Tyranael. Et Tyranael fut', tagged Yann Etienne, conducted by mail in January 2021, published 19 February 2021. The words appear verbatim inside the answer about what translating other authors taught her, in the aside about writing Kay's multiple viewpoints herself while translating.

Cabon's own page for Comme un diamant dans ma mémoire, Références section: the phrase is verbatim and names Le vêtement de A à Z by Sophie George (Falbalas), described as an illustrated encyclopedia of clothing styles across ages and civilisations. The page header gives the original title A Brightness Long Ago (2019).

verdicts.trueWording: m'a permis de résoudre bien des énigmes liées aux légendes chinoises
verdicts.note: Cabon's own page for Les Chevaux célestes, Références section; the subject of the verbatim clause is the dictionary Chinese Mythology A to Z by Jeremy Roberts. The page header gives the original title Under Heaven (2010).

verdicts.trueWording: efforcé de garder à l'esprit pendant mes propres travaux
verdicts.note: Cabon's own page for Le Fleuve céleste (original title River of Stars, 2013), last line of the Références section, thanking Marie-Christine Guyon for pointing him to Jean-François Billeter's Trois essais sur la traduction. Strictly, what he says he kept in mind is the enriching illumination that this réflexion sur les difficultés de la traduction de la poésie chinoise gave him; the substance of the claim holds.
